01_dashboard.notes: All 25 containers (decision D22) are answered by one read service, App\Domain\Dashboard\Services\DashboardMetrics: each container resolves to ok (a figure from the company's own documents), empty (source exists, no rows yet) or unavailable (the source does not exist yet and the panel names the module that will fill it - 01-21 expiry was the live example of that honesty until §04-39 shipped, and it now reads the batch register (expired + expiring buckets from BatchService, valued from the valuation layers, window from inventory.expiry_alert_days) and falls back to empty when no dated batch holds stock). Nothing is estimated and no panel carries a fixture. Visibility is the module's own view permission (DashboardMetrics::PERMISSIONS), so a user who may not read invoices never sees invoice totals; GET /app/dashboard/widgets/{code} refuses the same containers the page hides. Reuses CustomerQuery::dueBuckets, PurchaseQuery::payablesAgeing/receiptsByDay, ReorderService::alertRows and LeaderboardQuery so a panel cannot disagree with the screen it links to. Deviations from the planned per-widget controllers/registry and dashboard.widget.* keys are recorded in the traceability file. Fixes a real defect: WidgetSeeder produced mixed-case container codes (Todays_Sales) while translations (widget.todays_sales), label keys and the dashboard metric map all key off lowercase slugs - codes are lowercase now and the seeder prunes containers outside the catalogue. 01-27 stays PARTIAL: the widget admin CRUD belongs to 12 Settings, still PLANNED.

03_purchase.notes: Purchasing core + purchase bills. Suppliers (03-01/02/04), purchase orders with server-derived totals and a two-permission approval (03-22/23/24), receipt-state facets (03-25), PO→GRN with a hard over-receipt guard (03-29), goods receipts as the only inbound stock path with idempotent postings and valuation at cost paid (03-32/33/36), batch capture (03-34), and bills: entry from a posted receipt or direct (03-45), payable created by approval (03-44/03-46), three-way match (PO↔GRN↔bill) computed, stored and displayed (03-50), supplier payables with ageing buckets (03-48 partial). Approval posts a real journal entry through posting_rules seeded by PurchaseCoreSeeder (Dr inventory 1140 for goods-backed bills or Purchases & Services 5225 for direct ones, Dr input tax 2120, Cr accounts payable 2110); the maker can never approve their own bill. Partial: contacts/bank/TIN on one record (03-05), fixed category vocabulary (03-06), payment terms without a schedule (03-11), spend without scoring (03-12), no outbox so no 'sent to supplier' state (03-24), KPIs without report routes (03-31), ageing without a report screen (03-48). Not started by design: purchase requests, amendments, print/outbox, bill payment recording/print/reports (03-47/49/51), supplier payments (03-52…03-58), returns (03-59…03-64), RFQ, import/LC and the report family. Approval uses the direct permission purchase.bills.approve / purchase.orders.approve, not the Workflow engine, and a three-way mismatch is recorded rather than blocked (no configurable tolerance yet). Supplier payments (03-47, 03-52) reuse the shared payments table (direction out, supplier_id) and the polymorphic payment_allocations rows: SupplierPaymentService refuses an unposted or settled bill, refuses more than the balance, returns the original payment for a repeated idempotency key, posts Dr Accounts Payable 2110 / Cr Cash in Hand 1110 or Bank Account 1120 through posting_rules (supplier_payment / supplier_payment_bank), and moves paid_amount / due_amount / status on the bill inside the same transaction. Payment history filters by voucher, supplier, method, date and the bill it settled. Advances (03-53), BEFTN (03-54), schedule (03-55), payment approval workflow (03-56), reminders (03-57) and report exports (03-58) are still missing, as are purchase returns and debit notes (03-59…03-64) — the only honest correction path for a posted receipt or bill. Purchase returns (03-59, 03-60, 03-61) close the loop: a return is raised from a posted receipt (lines prefilled with received / already returned / returnable), from an open bill (service or goods with no receipt on file) or standalone, and quantities are capped at received − already returned, so the same goods cannot be claimed twice. Approval moves stock out through PURCHASE_RETURN_OUT (stock-managed products only, idempotent per line) and posts the debit note through posting_rules: purchase_return_posted (Dr AP 2110, Cr Inventory 1140, Cr Tax Payable 2120) or purchase_return_expense_posted (Cr Purchases & Services 5225). When the return names a bill, the same transaction credits it through a new credited_amount column, so due = total − paid − credited and the bill's own balance keeps agreeing with accounts payable; a credit larger than the bill's outstanding balance is refused rather than becoming an unapplied debit note (03-63). Posted returns are immutable; only unposted ones can be cancelled, with a reason. Still missing: return shipment tracking (03-62), the GL-derived supplier ledger and statement (03-63/06-08/06-14), report exports (03-64), supplier advances/BEFTN/schedule (03-53…03-57). Bill ageing (03-48) is now a screen of its own: GET /app/purchase/payables groups every open bill by supplier with current / 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / 90+ columns from each bill's own due date (an undated bill is never late), a totals row and bucket filters, and the supplier profile and ledger show the same buckets for one supplier. Returns appear as credits in the supplier's account (03-63 partial) and are capped at the bill they correct.

04_inventory.notes: Packaging DONE (§04-59/60/61/62) — the inventory half of a domain that only had its dispatch half. Types register on the existing packaging_types table: a type maps a name the floor uses onto a real stock-managed product, checked in the request and again in the service; identity (code and product) freezes once the type has consumed anything, because the consumption already priced what it took; a used type is retired rather than deleted so the movements that priced it are not orphaned; and the register reports when a live type stopped being usable. Packaging stock reads the same ledger (stock_balances + remaining layers) with 'lasts about' from the rate the type is actually consumed at, and a warehouse nobody delivered packaging to has no row rather than a zero. Packaging cost keeps two averages apart on purpose — shelf value against what went out cost, the latter from the layer that priced each consumption. The monthly report groups month × type with quantity and unit cost on every row, so a dearer month can be told from a busier one, and exports the same rows as CSV. Two keys (inventory.packaging, inventory.packaging.manage), four menu leaves, and the inventory report family gained /app/reports/inventory/packaging. Inventory 48/63, totals 261/619. Settings engine corrected while reviewing §04-20: a select is validated with Rule::in(array_keys(options)), so the cost-method field is now a value-to-label map (a bare list rendered 0..3 and refused every real method name), and every boolean switch carries the off in a hidden twin, because an unchecked box sends nothing and the engine only writes the keys it is handed - before this, a switch could be turned on but never off. Reorder desk DONE (§04-55/56/58) — the alert list now carries demand (real outbound movements only, per product per warehouse, over reorder.demand_window_days) with days of cover beside the level; the reorder desk proposes one quantity from one explainable ladder (policy answer as floor, demand over the lead time + safety as the need, the maximum as a ceiling, open purchase orders subtracted) and writes the proposal down before a purchase order exists, superseding the earlier row for the same shelf rather than stacking; accepting drafts through PurchaseOrderService and posts nothing, strict_auto_mode refuses to draft, and the history keeps every answer with the figures stored that day. Inventory 44/63, totals 257/619. Pick lists and putaway lists DONE (§04-44): the two instructions goods follow inside a warehouse, and neither of them holds a balance. A pick list is written for an order (each line's undelivered quantity) or by hand; its lines name the product's pick face and, for batch-tracked goods under FEFO, the earliest-expiring batch that still has stock. It finishes the walk without touching the ledger - dispatch still moves stock, which the tests pin - while moving the order to ready_to_ship when the state machine allows it. A putaway list is written from a posted receipt and writes its answer back as a bin assignment: the first home a product gets in a warehouse becomes its pick face, a later pallet landing elsewhere is recorded (placed_bin_id beside the planned bin) without moving it, and a quantity without a bin is refused, because directions are the only thing bin rows are for. Guards: one open walk per order, one live putaway per receipt, never more picked or placed than asked, nothing finished empty, and a putaway is finished only when the dock is empty. Ten audit actions, document types pick_list/putaway_list (PL/PA), two menu leaves under Inventory > Warehouse, and the storekeeper and manager roles gained warehouses.view/update - the layout is the warehouse, so the work in it shares its keys. Product settings DONE (§04-20): four keys in the inventory settings group, each with a consumer - default_cost_method preselects the add-product form (a stored value that is not a real method falls back to WAC rather than preselecting something the select cannot show), default_is_stocked and default_track_batch set the two switches, and sku_from_code makes a blank SKU mean ‘use the code’, which changes the required/derived handling in StoreProductRequest and UpdateProductRequest and drops the form's required flag. Defaults are a preselection, never a decision: every value is still overridable per product. Deliberately NOT scheduled and left PLANNED: product SEO (04-19) - there is no public storefront, so slugs and meta screens would be screens nobody reads. Also still PLANNED: variants (04-08), product unit conversion (04-09 - the unit master is real but nothing resolves a purchase unit to a base unit at the ledger edge, and that resolution belongs at the ledger edge or nowhere) and digital downloads (04-18 - a paid-order entitlement and a controlled file route, not a field on the form). Also corrected in the traceability: rows 04-01/02/03 listed product_variants as a DB entity, and no such table exists (04-08 attribute/variant work is still PLANNED). Catalogue import/export DONE (§04-12): the screen offers preview and import as two decisions on one code path (a preview rolls each row's transaction back, so its report is what a real run would do), each row is its own unit of work so a bad line is reported with its line number while the rest of the file lands, blank cells mean leave-it-alone rather than erase, masters are never invented from a spreadsheet, and 5000-row/2048 KB caps bound the work. Every run - previews included - leaves a product_imports row with the file, the actor, the counts, the columns read and the per-row errors, and a real run is audited as inventory.products_imported; a cost moved by an import still writes product_cost_history with the file named as the reason, because bulk is not a way around the trail. The export streams ProductImportService::COLUMNS, so an export can be edited and imported back - the tests pin that a round trip changes nothing. Two new permission keys (inventory.products.import/export) and three menu leaves (product import / product export / import history) are wired. Product cluster DONE (§04-04/05/06/10/14): DuplicateProduct copies the catalogue row and nothing else - no stock, layers, movements, barcode or cost history - behind inventory.products.create, audited as inventory.product_duplicated with stock_copied false, with a suggested identity that is actually free. Product categories are a real tree on the generic masters registry (MasterCatalog hierarchy flag): the parent select is database-backed and withdraws the row plus its descendants, the cycle guard refuses self-parenting and descent under its own child, a parent from another company is refused, a row with children cannot be deleted, and the flat list shows the parent name and the depth. Brands and units are DONE as served by the masters registry rather than a duplicated controller - but units are only PARTLY served: the unit master carries base_unit and conversion_factor and there is no unit_conversions table and no conversion at the ledger edge, so 04-09 stays PLANNED rather than claiming a conversion the ledger does not perform. Cost history: product_cost_history is append-only, ProductService::update writes a row with old/new standard cost, old/new cost method, reason and author only when the figure or the method actually moves, a method change still never rewrites a posted layer, the register says when each cost last moved, and the per-product screen shows the trail beside the valuation layers it is not. Price history gained a per-product screen on the same render path as the general history. Reading half of stock, plus the damage & loss family. Alerts: ReorderService::alertRows() judges each product against the policy that governs it in that warehouse (a warehouse row beats the company-wide row); a product with no active policy is deliberately never listed. A damage entry (04-46) moves goods into the damaged compartment with no valuation effect - reversible with a release; a loss entry (04-47) consumes the layers and posts Dr Inventory Loss & Damage 5260 / Cr Inventory 1140 through the stock_loss_posted rule; a write-off (04-48) is the document that removes value, raised against a compartment and approved by a second person (self-approval refused in the service), restating each line to the cost the ledger actually consumed; 04-49 values every statement from stock_layers, never an estimate; 04-51 reports the cost by kind/cause/warehouse/month with the damaged compartment valued at what a write-off would remove. The ledger state machine moved to StockMovement::applyDelta() - one definition shared by post, rebuild and the ledger view - and an outbound move from the damaged compartment no longer decrements on_hand a second time. 04-50 (insurance claims) stays PLANNED: it needs an insurance register nothing else in the system carries. 04-31 (stock count / cycle count) is built: a sheet snapshots the balance each line is asked about, counting is blind for anyone who cannot post, posting makes the counted figure the truth for the counted lines (the delta is measured against stock now, not the snapshot, so movement during the count is visible rather than smoothed) and writes the difference as one stock adjustment through PostStockAdjustment::post — the same path a manual adjustment takes. An uncounted line is left alone, a cancelled sheet corrects nothing and a posted sheet is closed. Posting carries its own permission (inventory.counts.post) because counting and changing the books are different jobs. 04-28 (transfer approval) is built on the same shape as 04-26 and with a stricter consequence: an approved transfer becomes a *draft*, so the two-leg lifecycle is untouched and a waiting transfer cannot be dispatched at all — the gate is a refusal in `dispatch()`, not a hidden button. Threshold `inventory.transfer_approval_above` (default 0), value frozen in `total_value` (a line with no cost is valued at source cost), maker ≠ checker, rejection terminal and needing a reason, audits transfer_submitted/approved/rejected. 04-26 (adjustment approval and history) is built: the approval lives on the document rather than in a generic request table, the threshold comes from the inventory settings (default 0 = everything posts as before), a document at or above it is stored pending_approval with no movements behind it, maker and checker must differ, approval applies the lines once through the same write the immediate path uses, a rejection needs a reason and moves nothing, and the history screen reads the whole life of the document off its own row. 04-42/04-43/04-45 (warehouse, its zones and bins, and the map) are built on the warehousing surface that already existed at /app/warehouses: a warehouse belongs to a branch and its code is unique there; the code may be renamed but the branch cannot change once the warehouse has moved stock, because stock is reported branch by branch, and a warehouse that has moved stock cannot be switched off or deleted at all because the ledger points at it; one default per branch is enforced in the service, so making a warehouse the default demotes the previous one. Zones carry a purpose (receiving/storage/picking/packing/dispatch/returns), bins live inside a zone and know their warehouse, and exactly one primary pick face per product per warehouse is enforced in the service (assigning a new one demotes the old). An empty zone is the only zone that can be removed and a bin with products still pointed at it cannot. The map is rendered from rows, and it names placements no movement has touched for 60 days. Bins record where, never how much: quantities stay in the ledger per product per warehouse. Batches and expiry (04-37…04-41) are built now. A batch is a label on the valuation layer: stock_layers.stock_batch_id is the link, so the register's remaining quantity and value are the ledger's own figures read through a correlated subselect and cannot drift from stock. The one inbound path resolves the batch (StockLedgerService::resolveBatch): a batch-tracked product must name its batch, an outbound movement never invents one, and a later receipt only fills a *blank* date in. Moving a date that is already recorded is a correction with a mandatory reason, kept as a trail row (stock_batch_expiry_changes: before, after, who, why) plus the audit event inventory.batch_expiry_corrected - so "the label says next year" and "the label was quietly moved to next year" are never confused; corrections are refused for another company's batch with a 404 and never touch stock. FEFO is an ordering inside ValuationService::consume(), not a second allocator: for a batch-tracked product the earliest-expiring layer leaves first and undated layers last, behind inventory.fefo_picking (default on) - switching it off falls back to the product's valuation method (FIFO/LIFO), and both orders are tested. The expiry desk lists expired, expiring and undated stock with stock still on hand (an expired batch nobody has any of is history, not a risk), states its alert window (inventory.expiry_alert_days, default 30) and shows the totals per bucket; erp:inventory:expiry-alerts sends one digest per state to the holders of inventory.batch.manage, deduped per state per recipient per day. 04-41 reuses the write-off document that already exists (the desk hands the batch over with product, quantity and an expiry reason prefilled) instead of adding a second way to destroy value. 04-37 is DONE for the batch half only: serial tracking is NOT built (track_serial exists on products, the menu leaf stays planned - a table nobody writes to would be a fake), FefoAllocator/ExpiryQuery do not exist as classes, and the plan's per-category FEFO strictness is not implemented. Barcodes, QR codes and the label desk DONE (§04-13/04-52/04-53/04-54), and the encoders are this application's own: BarcodeService writes Code 128 (subsets B and C, check character computed from the position weights, the quiet zone part of the output, 0.25 mm minimum module from ISO/IEC 15417) and QrService writes byte-mode QR for levels L/M/Q/H across all 40 versions (bit buffer with terminator and pad bytes, Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8/0x11D) with a built generator polynomial, the standard's function patterns, the zigzag placement, the eight masks scored by the standard's penalties, BCH-protected format and version information). Both emit SVG - no barcode or image library is installed, and SVG is what a label wants anyway. Both were verified by decoding with other people's decoders rather than by assertion: eight Code 128 symbols read back exactly by ZXing; eight QR symbols read back exactly by jsQR and ZXing; the QR matrix, version choice and mask identical to a reference implementation's. That process found two real defects that would have printed unreadable labels: a zigzag loop that wrote its timing-column shift back into its own counter (infinite loop), and drawFormatBits/drawVersionBits taking the function map by value, so the format area was never marked as function modules and drawCodewords overwrote it. LabelService owns the payload and the paper: what a label encodes is the row's own code (barcode, else SKU, else product code - never a row id and never a token minted at print time, so the same box prints the same bars next year), the price shown is the price the till resolves through PricingService, and the geometry is real millimetres (A4 3x8 = 3x70 by 8x37 mm exactly filling the page, A4 3x7 and two thermal rolls). The desk is told when a code would print below the standard's floor; the QR is what gives way, because the bars are what the warehouse scanner reads, and the warning stays on the screen - printed on a label it would ruin the label it warns about. A generated sheet is filed like any other document (DocumentRenderer::renderLabelSheet -> storeGenerated with a nullable owner, because a sheet spans many rows and none of them owns it, and a nullable branch, because no branch in context means a company-wide sheet and never branch 0), is served back from the stored file rather than re-rendered (a checksum over a re-render is a checksum of nothing), and is registered as label_sheet with requires_numbering false because nothing downstream refers to "label sheet 12". Every print and reprint is logged with user, IP and copies. The scanner bench takes the same keyboard-wedge input the till does and resolves codes through one method (InventoryLabelController::resolve) so the bench, the desk and the counter cannot disagree; it matches a product's barcode, SKU or code, then a batch number, and reports a code under the configured floor as half a barcode rather than as not-found. New permission inventory.products.print (the symbol is a thing you print, not a thing you read), the settings groups labels and barcode each have a consumer (which paper the desk defaults to, which way the counters read), and the catalogue's Barcode & QR leaves are mapped: product barcode / generate barcode -> /app/inventory/labels/barcodes, product qr code / generate qr code -> /app/inventory/labels/qr-codes, print labels -> the desk, label templates -> /app/settings/labels, barcode scanner setup -> the scanner bench, barcode settings -> /app/settings/barcode. Tests: LabelDeskTest pins the payload order, the filed-bytes == served-bytes identity, the checksum, the reprint log, the cross-company refusal, the page fill (25 labels over two sheets), the too-narrow warning and the dropped-QR note, the generator screens and the SVG endpoints, and the scanner's four resolutions. Inventory 52/63, totals 265/619.

08_cash_bank.notes:
The money desk (§08-01/02/03/04/06/07/11): the registry of accounts money sits in IS the chart of accounts — `accounts` gained `instrument` (cash|bank|wallet), `bank_name`, `account_number` and `wallet_provider`, backfilled from the `is_cash`/`is_bank` flags the standard COA already carries, so declaring an account creates a real postable leaf under Current Assets and the registry and the ledger can never be two lists. Nothing on these screens stores a balance: every position is one grouped query over posted journal_lines per account and per branch, a negative drawer is flagged rather than hidden, and each account's book is `LedgerService::accountLedger()` filtered to it — the same ledger the general-ledger screen renders, opening brought forward, running balance per row, and the identical rows streamed as CSV for statement matching. Money moves through one service and three numbered documents: a receipt (Dr the account it landed in, Cr what it was for, money_receipt/MR), a payment (Dr the cost, Cr the account it left, expense_voucher/EX) and a transfer between the company's own accounts (Dr the destination, Cr the source, one entry for the pair, its own cash_transfer/CT type and table). Both sides are always named by the operator rather than resolved from a rule, because the person holding the bank SMS is the only one who knows which account the money landed in; all three carry a unique (company, idempotency_key), so a retried request moves money once; every posting goes through JournalPostingService; a money account cannot be the counter account of a receipt or a payment (that is a transfer, and the refusal says so); an account may be renamed and re-described freely but its code and its instrument are fixed once money has moved through it, since changing a bank into a cash account regroups every report ever printed instead of correcting a typo; and an account holding a balance cannot be closed, because that is the one state from which nobody can say where the cash went. Opening a mobile wallet is a separate permission (`wallets.accounts`) from opening a bank account, and wallet reconciliation is manual with the screen saying so — no provider adapter is pretended to exist. Nine permission keys for the module (`cash.view`, `cash.receipts.create`, `cash.payments.create`, `cash.transfers`, `bank.accounts`, `bank.view`, `wallets.accounts`, `bank.reconcile`, `wallets.reconcile`) across twenty-nine routes, with fourteen catalogue leaves mapped — a leaf that lands on an account list rather than on a page that cannot open without an account id, because a menu entry must never be a dead link (the cheque, expense, petty-cash and report leaves stay PLANNED and unmapped for that reason). `bank.reconcile` is separate from `bank.view`: reading a book and putting your signature on a proof are different jobs. `CashBankDeskTest` pins the position coming from the books, the balanced entries and their series, both transfer legs with a retried transfer moving the money once, the refusals (self-transfer, non-money account, funded close, closed account), the book and its CSV, and the wallet permission. The second slice is the desk that proves the first one (§08-08/09/12): `bank_statement_imports` / `bank_statement_lines` read a statement export whole file or nothing — one unreadable row refuses the file, names the row number and stores no line, a labelled brought-forward or period-total row is read and set aside rather than refused, the file is previewed before it is imported, and a run that stored nothing carries no checksum so the unique (company, account, checksum) index refuses the same statement twice while a preview and a later real import stay legal — and `bank_reconciliations` / `reconciliation_lines` freeze the period: both openings and closings, the unmatched totals on each side, the counts, and `difference`, which is the period's unexplained opening gap (statement opening against book opening). That is why the desk refuses to pretend: a hand-made pair must be the same amount, so naming a leftover restates the lists and cannot move the number, and the screen says exactly that; the closing figure the clerk typed can be corrected while the period is open (the commonest failure is reading it off the wrong row), the bank's own opening figure is read off its running balance rather than derived from the typed closing figure, a reconciliation cannot be signed off until it adds up, the preparer is never the signer, and a signed period is history — not re-matched, not restated, and not picked up by a later reconciliation. Wallet reconciliation is the same machinery under `wallets.reconcile` with the screen stating that no provider API is connected instead of shipping a button that could not work. Three routes carry the module floor and the instrument's own key is asserted in the controller, because the instrument lives on the account and not in the URL. `ReconciliationDeskTest` pins whole-or-nothing with the row named, the desk's own template round-tripping through its own reader, the leftovers explaining the gap, an opening disagreement refused a signature, the closing figure corrected while open, a signed period frozen, and the wallet's separate keys. Totals 275/619. §08-13/08-14: the cheque register and the printed record of a cheque. cheques (the slip number unique per company+account+direction, both directions, post-dated by date); ChequeService — nothing posts until a bank pays it, one posting call inside clear(), a bounce after clearing reverses the original entry and a bounce before it posts nothing, post-dated refused early, clearing through a money account only with a money counter account refused as a transfer; ChequeController (register/detail/transition/print) with cheques.view, cheques.manage, cheques.clear and cheques.print as separate powers; AmountInWords (English and Bangla, lakh/crore, bnFigures) behind the printed record, filed through DocumentRenderer::storeGenerated/recordPrint under the unnumbered `cheque` document type; ChequeDeskTest; the six catalogue leaves map onto one filtered register. The expense desk (§08-15…§08-18) is built on one refusal — this module never guesses a ledger account: an `expense_categories` row IS a GL account (only a postable expense leaf of the same company may be chosen, and a category is deactivated rather than deleted), an expense credits either the account the money actually left or payables resolved through the company's own `expense_posted` posting rule, and `settled_with` keeps paid and owed distinct. Above the approval limit (`cash.expense_approval_above`) the expense waits with no journal entry at all, and the threshold it was judged against is stored on the row so a later change cannot rewrite what a past signature was for; the person who recorded an expense can never decide it (`ExpenseService`), and reversing a posted expense writes the answering entry instead of editing the original. Four keys separate reading the register, recording an expense, approving one and re-pointing a category; four catalogue leaves map onto the register and the mapping screen. ExpenseDeskTest; the recurring desk (§08-19) keeps the same refusal one step into the future — `recurring_expenses` stores a schedule (payee, amount, frequency, day_of_month, next_due_on) and writing one posts nothing, because a plan is not a payment. On the day, `RecurringExpenseService` writes an ordinary expense through `ExpenseService`, so the approval gate, the category-is-an-account rule and the reversal path all still apply and automation is never a way round a signature: the actor is the schedule's author, who is therefore the one person who cannot approve what it produced. The date advances exactly once and the unique `expenses_recurring_unique` (schedule, date) pair makes a second run an adoption rather than a second month of rent; a monthly schedule clamps to the end of a short month (31st → 28th in February → 31st in March); a refusal (an inactive category) leaves the date where it was so the month stays visibly unpaid instead of being skipped; a last date stops the schedule itself; the daily `erp:cash:recurring-expenses` command does the same work headless and reports what it generated and refused. Permission `expenses.recurring`, with generation additionally needing `expenses.create`; the catalogue leaf maps onto the desk. RecurringExpenseDeskTest. Petty cash (08-21) is built on the same money path seen through a much smaller hole: `PettyCashService` gives a float its own postable cash leaf under Current Assets with a named custodian, pays vouchers out of that account through `MoneyMovementService::pay()` so a tin can never pay money it does not hold, asks for the money first when a voucher is at or above the company's own petty cash limit — a waiting request posts nothing and cannot be approved by the person who asked — and treats replenishment as a transfer into the float rather than a second record of the spending. A float holding cash, or one carrying a waiting request, cannot be closed. Four keys (pettycash.funds|spend|approve|replenish) keep the jobs apart, the four catalogue leaves are mapped, and PettyCashDeskTest covers the lot. The two PLANNED rows here are cash count (08-05) and the report family (08-20, 08-22). The cash count desk is the one screen in this module that does not believe the ledger: the expected figure is the ledger balance on the day of the count, frozen onto the row with the tolerance it was judged against; only the difference posts (through the `cash_count_variance` rule, `cash_short` 5250 / `cash_over` 4200); an exact count posts nothing; a variance at or above `cash.cash_count_tolerance` waits unposted for somebody other than the counter; the denominations written down must add up to the counted figure.

§08-10 bank charge auto-posting: a rule is a tariff, not a posting — writing one charges nothing, and the run posts what has come due as two lines and no party (Dr the bank-charge expense, Cr the account the money left, through `JournalPostingService::post()`, `source_type` `bank_charge`, its own numbered series BC). A commission is computed on the posted credits of the account since its last charge and the turnover, rate and basis are frozen onto the row; a commission in a quarter when nothing left the account is refused rather than posted at zero. `unique(rule_id, charged_on)` makes a second charge for the same day impossible, so a scheduled run that overlaps a manual record adopts the row it finds; a rule whose last date has passed stops itself; pause stops the charges and resume starts from the next occurrence; a wrong charge is reversed once, never edited; recording a charge (`bank.charges`) and writing the rules that post them (`bank.charges.rules`) are separate powers. `erp:cash:bank-charges` runs daily at 06:10 per active company with `--company`/`--dry-run`.

§08-20/§08-22 report family (closing §08 at 22/22): the expense report counts posted expenses only — pending ones have no journal entry and are named in a footnote instead of being counted — and proves its tie to the ledger by comparing its total with the debit the categories' accounts carry, naming any difference per account rather than absorbing it; filters by category, branch, paid-or-owed, search and window, CSV with a labelled totals block. The cash reports: the book is the account's own ledger with the opening brought forward and the closing taken from the account (not added up from the rows), the bank book is the same for every bank and wallet, the cash flow is built from the counterpart account of every posting on a money account with own-account transfers reported apart and excluded from income, and the inflow/outflow groups add up to the money accounts' own debit and credit totals. The session variance is the one page that is not the ledger's and says so on screen: expected = float + cash sales + cash in − cash out, frozen on the session; an open session shows no counted figure. `expenses.reports` and `cash.reports` are separate read-only keys.

11_marketing.notes: The marketing desk is open and the four channel groups are one desk rather than four controllers. `CampaignService::resolveTransport()` is the only place that decides whether anything can be sent: an SMS campaign needs an active `SmsProvider` with `config_status = configured`, an email campaign needs a real `mail.default` (`log`/`array`/empty are all no transport), and WhatsApp and push have no adapter, so their messages are written as held with the reason. Nothing in the module writes `sent` — a message is `queued`, `not_configured` or `failed`, and a failure keeps the transport's own words in `last_error`. The audience (`all|recent_buyers|dormant|manual` + `audience_days`) is expanded on the day of launch; anybody it does not reach is a recipient row with `skip_reason` (`opted_out|no_address|blacklisted`) and no message, and the counts above the table come from the same pass as the rows. Rows 12-01…12-08 (company/branch), 12-11 (meetings), 12-14 (assets & vehicles), 12-15 (utility bills) and 12-16 (visitors) remain PLANNED. §12-11 meetings: `meetings`/`meeting_attendees`/`meeting_events` plus `tasks.meeting_id`, so an action item is a task rather than a second to-do list (it lands on the board and in “my tasks” with the same states, events and notifications). The diary refuses a slot already taken by somebody on the list, names the person and the meeting, and records a deliberate overlap via `allow_clash`; the life cycle is ordered (`scheduled → held → minuted`), attendance and minutes are refused before the meeting has happened, empty minutes are refused rather than stored, cancelling needs a reason and is final, and a move keeps the time it moved from in `meeting_events.meta`. Invites/moves/cancellations/published minutes notify once per meeting per person, and `erp:business:meeting-reminders` (every fifteen minutes) reminds each person once, ever, skipping declined invitations. §12-14 assets & vehicles: one `business_assets` table read four ways (register, vehicle management, equipment, trip log) with `business_asset_events` as the history and `vehicle_trips` as the runs, and a vehicle modelled as an asset that carries plates rather than as a second table. Every figure on those pages is derived: book value is cost less `accumulated_depreciation`, and that column moves only with a posted journal entry — the monthly run posts Dr 5270 / Cr 1590 per asset per completed month, dated the last day of the month it covers, `source_event` `asset_depreciation_{Y-m}`, so re-running the same month finds its own entry (the lookup runs without the global branch scope: a charge posted by another branch is still the same charge) and catches up missed months one entry each; depreciation starts from `depreciation_starts_on ?? capitalised_at ?? acquired_on`, waits for capitalisation, respects the salvage floor and never charges a month before it has ended. A trip's distance comes from the odometer (blank stays blank) and a cost per kilometre is only shown when there is a distance. Three shelves (`AssetRegistry::SHELVES`), a condition and a status read as labels, a disposal that keeps its date, reason and proceeds (and never posts — the ledger entry is the accountant's), papers linked to the §12-03 registers rather than re-typed, `erp:business:asset-depreciation` (monthly, day 1, 06:40) that also runs `--dry-run`, and two permission rows (`business.assets.view` / `.manage`). §12-15 utilities: `utility_providers` (code, family, consumer number, meter, premises, due day and — the column that earns its keep — the expense account its bills belong in, defaulted from the family: 5230 utilities, 5220 rent) and `utility_bills` (period month, issue/due dates, amount, consumption and its unit, life cycle `recorded|pending_approval|paid|void`, the approval gate's threshold and decision, `paid_on`, `money_account_id` and `journal_entry_id`). Recording posts nothing; paying posts exactly one entry (Dr the provider's account, Cr the account the money left, `source_type utility_bill`, `source_event utility_bill_paid`) and the register keeps the entry number; at or above `cash.expense_approval_above` the payment is held for a second signature (maker ≠ checker), a rejection returns the bill to unpaid with nothing moved, and a paid bill can never be voided. Overdue and due-soon are read from the clock (`DUE_SOON_DAYS = 14`), a second bill for the same provider and month is refused naming the existing one, the six default counterparties are materialised only where a company has none, bills are `UB-000001` per company, the six menu leaves are one screen filtered by `family`, and `erp:business:utility-reminders` (daily 07:00) digests overdue and due-soon once per company per day. §12-16 visitors: `visitors` (name, phone, organisation, the paper shown, and the blacklist with its reason) and `visitor_visits` (branch, host, `scheduled_for`, purpose, badge, wait place, items, vehicle, life cycle `expected|inside|out|no_show|cancelled`, the two timestamps and who stamped them) — a booking is not an arrival (no badge, no time, nobody inside), checking in issues the day's next badge `VB-YYYYMMDD-NN` (unique per company) and notifies the host once by dedupe key, the blacklist is enforced in the service at the door and at the booking form and never written while the person is still inside, a booking for another day cannot be checked in today, a passed booking is closed as a no-show, dwell time is arithmetic on the two timestamps, people are one record each (matched on the phone) with one row per visit, ID numbers are masked on the register, the reports lens cuts the same rows by day, gate, host, purpose, status and repeat visitor, and `erp:business:visitor-watch` (daily 08:00) digests who is expected today and names any row left open from an earlier day. 16_cross_cutting.notes: The cross-cutting layer has started with the door a customer walks through: the invoice verification link (§16-19) and the page behind it (§16-20). The token is derived — 43 base64url characters of HMAC-SHA256 over `verification:{company}|{invoice}|{rotation}` — and the database holds only `hash('sha256', $token)`, so a read-only leak of the invoices table publishes nothing while a reprint still carries the same address. Rotation is a version bump (the old address 404s immediately), withdrawal keeps the date it happened, and `resolve()` re-derives the digest after the lookup so a hand-edited row cannot publish another document. The public page publishes the document and not the books: company/branch identity, number, date, lines, VAT/total/paid/due, payment state and who raised it — never the internal notes, the journal entry, the audit chain, costs or another customer — with contact details masked because a link can be forwarded, and warranty dates absent while cover was not registered anywhere — the page said so in words. §16-16 has since landed, so it now names the date the cover runs to (or ended on) and only falls back to “no cover period is registered” when that is what the register says. Every visit is one `public_access_logs` row (token **hash** in the column) plus a `sales.invoice_verified` audit event; the route is guest + `throttle:30,1`; publishing, rotating and withdrawing sit behind `sales.invoices.issue` and the paper's QR appears only when a link is live. `tests/Feature/InvoiceVerificationTest.php` — 13 tests / 155 assertions, green. Also built this slice: **the public document link (16-21) and its secure download (16-22)** — the same derived-and-hashed shape as the verification door (`HMAC-SHA256` over `document:{company}|{document}|{rotation}`, 43 base64url characters, only the digest stored), rotation as a version bump, withdrawal that keeps its date and takes the file back to `visibility = private` (so the foundation's own `allowsPublicAccessByToken` rule cannot disagree with the share flow), a permanent link being one with **no** expiry and an expiry bounded to 1…365 days, the download streamed from the private disk with the file's own MIME type and a filename that cannot climb out of a directory, and views and downloads recorded as different facts. `tests/Feature/DocumentShareTest.php` — 14 tests / 142 assertions green. Then **the reusable renderer, the title rule and the print history (16-23, 16-24, 16-25)**: twelve document types answer five questions in one table (`DocumentSourceRegistry` — title code, permission, loader, paper content, paper sizes), one shell renders them in A4 and on 80 mm thermal with the logo, seal and signature inlined, a watermark, English and Bengali label sets and paginated tables, `DocumentTitleService` enforces the title rule (INVOICE for a normal sale, a statutory form's own title otherwise, and a non-statutory type may not claim a tax title) and the conditional tax block (D10 — a zero VAT column is not printed), and every production files a versioned, checksummed copy plus a `print_history` row carrying the title, the paper, the copy locale, the watermark and the checksum, read back through `documents.view_history` at `/app/documents/print/{type}/{id}/history` and `/app/documents/print-log`. Printing needs the document's own key, per type. `payroll` and `payslip` are listed as not printable with the reason (§10 has no payroll run) rather than printing a blank sheet. `tests/Feature/DocumentRenderTest.php` — 11 tests / 129 assertions green. Two real defects on the documents desk were found while wiring it and fixed: the library page eager-loaded and printed a relation called `uploadedBy` that does not exist on the model (every visit to `/app/documents` returned 500), and `Document` had no `branch()` relation despite its `branch_id` column and branch scope. Also fixed while wiring the verification door: the orders bulk bar's invoice button said “Invoice” where the behaviour and its test both said “Print invoice”. Then **the audit platform itself (16-33, 16-34, 16-35)**: `AuditVocabulary` derives 28 modules from the 286 recorded action names (checked against the source tree in a test rather than kept by hand), translates the five legacy names (`reconcile`, `pay`, `escalate`, `print_*`, `notify_*`) on read only — those rows are hash-chained history — and lists the sensitive prefixes that §16-36 will route on. Recorder and verifier now share one canonical shape for timestamps and snapshots, without which **no chain had ever verified** (the writer hashed the company's wall-clock time, the reader hashed the model's UTC instant), and the viewer is scoped to the company and then to one *grouped* branch predicate — the old ungrouped `orWhere` with a `null` inside `whereIn` had admitted every company-wide row of every actor. An explicitly null branch is now recorded as company-wide instead of being silently replaced by the acting branch. `php artisan erp:audit:seal [--period=YYYY-MM] [--force]` seals a closed month only after the chain verifies, refuses a broken chain or an unfinished month, writes no empty seal and audits `security.audit_period_sealed`; `erp:chain-verify --archives` re-reads every seal, which is the only thing that can catch a row deleted from an old month; and “Verify now” records `security.chain_verified` with the verdict, because a check that writes nothing cannot be told apart from a page nobody opened. `tests/Feature/AuditPlatformTest.php` — 12 tests / 382 assertions green. The same test wave exposed a third defect: six of the twelve printable types were gated behind permission keys never checked against the seeder, one of which (`sales.payments.print`) did not exist at all — a census test now walks the renderer catalogue against the `permissions` table, and the missing key was seeded. **And the warranty register, fed by the delivery event itself (16-16, 16-17, 16-18).** A warranty is the promise in this application a customer can hold the company to, so cover comes from the product's own `product_warranties` row and a product with no policy is delivered with no cover at all — the register says “no policy” rather than inventing twelve months, because a default is a promise the company never made. Activation happens inside the delivery event's own transaction and is keyed on the delivered line (`UNIQUE (company, source_line_key)`), so a re-delivered challan or a retried request writes nothing — the test walks a challan back to `dispatched` and delivers it again to prove it — and where no challan carried the goods the invoice is the delivery event, refusing to promise twice what the challan already covered. The dates are fixed when cover starts: `ends_on` is the delivery day plus the policy's months, clamped, so a one-month cover begun on 31 January ends on the last day of February (and on 29 February in a leap year) instead of rolling into March; editing the policy afterwards moves nothing already granted. The **clock, not the column**, answers “is this covered”: `stateNow()` compares `ends_on` with today while `status` keeps the life cycle, which is why the register opens on its live lens. A claim never edits the cover — closing one means stating what was done (repair/replace/refund) by whom and at what cost, only an honoured resolution marks the cover `claimed`, and a cover that has run out or was withdrawn refuses a claim with its reason, because a goodwill repair is an expense rather than a warranty. The §07 catalogue leaves (`Warranty Returns | Processing | Completed`) and `Product Warranty Config` are pinned to the real screens, and the public verification page above was corrected where the new register made its old sentence false. `tests/Feature/WarrantyDeskTest.php` — 16 tests / 162 assertions green; the whole desk sits behind new keys `sales.warranties.view` and `sales.warranties.manage`, and every permission key the application asks for is now checked against the seeder (269 asked, 0 unseeded).
